Title: How stable are untrained CNNs? Measuring random-weight CNN variability on EEG with Fuzzy PyTorch
Leaders: Roy Seo (post-doc, Centre for Addiction and Mental Health / Krembil Centre NeuroInformatics) – email: seoroy15@gmail.com – Discord: royjoysoy
Collaborators: Yohan Chatelain, scientific associate, Centre for Addiction and Mental Health / Krembil Centre NeuroInformatics) - email: Yohan.Chatelain@camh.ca Mina Alizadeh, Ph.D. student mina.alizadeh94@gmail.com
Project Description:
Untrained CNNs use random weights. They are never trained. Yet they can still extract useful features from data, including EEG.

We want to understand them better. Our main question is simple: how much do untrained CNNs vary?

They can vary in two ways:

  • Different random weights (different seeds).
  • Small rounding errors in computer arithmetic.

To measure the second kind, we use Fuzzy PyTorch. It adds tiny random noise to floating-point math. This is called Monte Carlo Arithmetic (MCA). We run the same model many times and compare the outputs.

We will use open EEG datasets.

Who is this for?

  • Anyone curious about random weights and untrained CNNs.
  • Anyone who wants to know why they work on EEG, or why they don't.
  • Anyone who knows good open EEG datasets. Please tell us!

I am new to untrained CNNs too. We will learn together. By the end of Brainhack, we will all know a lot more.

Our goal is to write a short paper together. Everyone who helps will be credited.

Key resources:

  • Fuzzy PyTorch: Gonzalez-Pepe, Akhaddar, Glatard & Chatelain (2026). "Fuzzy PyTorch: Rapid Numerical Variability Evaluation for Deep Learning Models." TMLR. https://openreview.net/forum?id=0ogq232VGP
  • Verificarlo (the tool behind Fuzzy PyTorch): Denis, de Oliveira Castro & Petit (2016). "Verificarlo: Checking Floating Point Accuracy through Monte Carlo Arithmetic." IEEE ARITH.
Goals for Brainhack Montreal:
• Beginner: Find and list open EEG datasets we can use.
  • Beginner: Run an untrained CNN on one EEG dataset.
  • Intermediate: Compare results across different random seeds.
  • Intermediate: Run the same model with Fuzzy PyTorch (MCA) and measure the variability.
  • Advanced: Compare seed variability with MCA variability.
  • Final: Write a short paper draft together.
